transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Yeah, so, what brings me in is that... well, I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. Like, I'm a computer support specialist, and I'll start tracing a client's network problem. Usually, it's a DNS issue—honestly, it's almost always DNS. I was actually just telling my brother that. He bought this new mesh router for his house last weekend and couldn't get it to connect to his smart fridge. Which, honestly, why does a fridge even need Wi-Fi? It just tells you when you're out of milk, but I already know when I'm out of milk because I drink it every morning. I buy that almond kind, the vanilla one... wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Oh, right, work. So I'll be trying to fix this network problem, and ten minutes later I'll realize I've reread the exact same log entries three times and I still don't even know what they say. It's just getting really bad.
Have you experienced these struggles with focus and getting distracted since you were a child, or is this a more recent development in your life?

Oh, no, it's definitely not new. It's been my whole life, really. My mom actually still jokes about it. She kept all my old report cards from grade school—you know, the old thick paper ones? I think they used carbon paper back then. Man, I remember getting ink all over my hands from those old mimeograph machines they used for worksheets. The smell of that ink was incredible, honestly. I don't think kids today even know what that smells like, with everything being on iPads now. My nephew has an iPad for first grade, which just seems wild to me. 

But anyway, she pulls those old report cards out sometimes, and every single one basically says the same thing. They all said I was a bright kid, but that I just never stayed in my seat. And I was always blurting out answers. I had this one teacher, Mr. Harrison, who used to get so mad when I'd answer before he finished speaking. He drove this awful brown station wagon with the fake wood paneling on the side... wait, what was I saying? 

Right, the report cards. Yeah, they also always said I lost my homework. Which drove me absolutely crazy, because I actually *did* the homework! I'd finish it, put it somewhere, and then it would just vanish. Just totally gone. Sort of like my car keys now, actually. I bought one of those Bluetooth trackers for my keys last month, but the battery died and I keep forgetting to buy the little coin batteries for it. They're CR2032s, I think, but I always end up buying the 2025s by mistake...
